question: What rules apply to Medicaid eligibility?

results.text: The Medicaid eligibility final rule at 435.110, 435.116 and 435.118 set forth the mechanism for consolidating certain federal eligibility categories into four main groupings: adults, children, pregnant women and parents/caretaker relatives. The table provided below lays out the consolidation of mandatory and optional eligibility groups (a version of this table was also included as part of the preamble to the proposed rule). Yes. Eligibility rules for Medicaid is going to vary by state. Medicaid can help pay for services and costs that Medicare doesn't cover. When you have both programs, Medicare pays first and Medicaid will pay second.If you qualify for Medicaid in your state, you automatically qualify for extra help paying for your Medicare Part D prescription drug coverage.
